newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy closer to single currency than yr ago-Monti.
newsitem.headline: Italy closer to single currency than yr ago-Monti.

text.p: Italy is closer to meeting requirements for joining the single currency than it was a year go but lasting structural measures are still needed, European Union commissioner Mario Monti said on Monday.

Monti, speaking to reporters at a conference on Europe, said Italy's membership of EMU from the outset in 1999 was "a possibility that has increased notably since September 1996 when the government set itself the aim."
"The goal is still absolutely possible," added the commissioner for the internal market.
However, Monti said the government needed to carry out measures "that are perceived to be structural and lasting" and referred to the urgent need of welfare spending reforms.

"I hope that it becomes increasingly clear that those who oppose these measures in the name of looking after the interests of the weakest are in reality making the situation of the weakest more serious," he said.
